name: roll-and-drain
description: Serve a ball (bd_trough eject) and autolaunch it at full strength. With the plunge-routing fix (col_loop_r_deflector re-sited, col_loop_top shortened -- see notes) the ball crosses the top of the table, descends the LEFT side through the shot map and arrives at the left flipper, where this golden's recorded press (tick 8956, released 9556) genuinely meets it: at the contact tick the bat stands at 90.79 deg -- its driven end-of-stroke pose -- instead of its 141.00 deg rest pose, the ball leaves that contact with a measurably different velocity, and it drains 62 ticks sooner than the same run with the press removed. Real gameplay input only (no manual ball placement); traced and verified deterministic this pass.

notes: stateHash() hashes the whole game tree, which includes machine.deviceSlots -- this golden therefore freezes the LOOP-WRITTEN value of deviceSlots (sim/loop/index.ts:326-329, the live AD-7 violation tracked as DW-70) as part of its reference hash. If Story 2.5's fix is faithful the values will be identical and nothing breaks; if this golden ever breaks on deviceSlots alone, check DW-70 before assuming the physics changed. Story 2.1b (2026-09-01): header.tableHash/assetHash refreshed (bd_lock's new deviceSlots entry -- see the sibling goldens' own notes). Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01), correcting this note: the sentence that used to stand here -- blaming "Blender's alphabetical bpy.data.objects ordering" reshuffling existing nodes' own array positions, with an "order-sensitive broadphase" -- was investigated and found FALSE, twice: the collision document is alphabetically sorted throughout, so the ~28 new names interleave among the existing ones rather than reshuffling their relative order, and a document rebuilt with the rework's own wall-height and deflector changes reverted reproduces the two affected goldens bit-identically, ruling out node reordering as the mechanism. The TRUE cause of the two affected goldens' own trajectory divergence was not identified by either the implement pass or this rework; DW-53's wall-height change (col_wall_left/_top/_right/_lane now reaching the glass) and DW-58's col_lane_deflector removal were both tested and ruled out individually (each reproduces the divergence bit-identically when reverted alone). State plainly rather than guess further: the trajectory changed because the shot map's own regeneration changed the collision document in some way this investigation did not isolate -- not because of the specific mechanism previously claimed here. expectedHash/expectedGameStateHash were refreshed to the current, correctly-computed values for the UNCHANGED (byte-identical) recorded transitions/coilPrologue/durationTicks. FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED: re-verifying this golden's own scenario claim against the refreshed run found the claim no longer holds within the recorded durationTicks -- this story's own Boundaries & Constraints treats a durationTicks (or scenario-assertion) change as a Block If, so this implementation pass halted short of that change and left the affected test(s) red rather than silently widening the window or the threshold. See this implementation pass's own final report for the measured detail. Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01): re-verified against the geometry this pass actually shipped (the flat-topped-body bevels and the DRAGON-bank backstop wall, task list items 1-3 -- none of which lie anywhere near this golden's own trajectory, confirmed by inspection: the ball never leaves y < 450 the whole run). The scenario claim still does not hold within the recorded durationTicks (8200): the served ball is still in play at the tick bound (measured this pass: x = 447.37, y = 191.04, still descending at ~975 mm/s). Measured directly this pass (extending the SAME recorded transitions/coilPrologue past durationTicks, nothing else changed): the ball keeps descending and drifting slowly leftward along the sloped bottom-wall face (DW-119's own mechanism, working as designed) until it crosses into the drain aperture's own x-range (DRAIN_X0_MM..DRAIN_X1_MM) and drains for real, between tick 8640 (x = 314.9, y = -57.0, not yet drained) and tick 8650 (drained) -- 440-450 ticks past the recorded window, roughly 5% longer than recorded. This is unrelated to the shot map (confirmed above) and remains a genuine Block If per this story's own Boundaries & Constraints: the fix is real (the ball does drain) but landed outside a duration this story is not authorised to widen. Left red for the lead, with this measurement in hand rather than a re-investigation from zero. Rework iteration 3 (2026-09-02, DW-121 / answer A/C): re-recorded under the narrow exception (this story's Spec Change Log) after the plunge-routing fix -- col_loop_r_deflector re-sited steeper (theta ~55.8 deg) so a plunged ball clears the Right Loop's own entrance instead of rattling in its pocket, and col_loop_top shortened at its own LEFT end (to x = 220, clear of both loops' own rails and inside the x-range test/shot-routing.test.ts's own descending-release sweep already proves handles a falling ball) so a crossing ball detaches into the open interior field -- the Dragon's legs, the DRAGON bank and the Ramp -- rather than sliding into the Left Loop's own lane, which returns to the OUTLANE, not the inlane (the defect Story 2.1c owns, not this story). Traced against the real runReplay() harness with this golden's own unchanged coilPrologue (serve + full autolaunch at tick 5021): the ball crosses the top by tick ~5700 (max y = 1053.3), descends through the shot-map bodies, reaches the flipper-reachable band (y in (40,145), x in (140,375)) repeatedly between roughly tick 8800 and 10200 (closest approach to the left bat's own tip, 20.4 mm, at tick 10173), and drains for real -- WITH NO FLIPPER INPUT AT ALL -- between tick 10343 and 10344, confirmed by a full bd_trough (4/4 slots) and ballsInPlay = 0. The OLD transitions (a left-flipper press at tick 5041, held for the rest of the run) matched the OLD table's much shorter, obstruction-free crossing time and are no longer meaningful against this table's shot map, so transitions are now empty (this is within the granted exception's own "re-record", not a header-only refresh) and durationTicks widened to 10400 (comfortably past the measured drain at 10344) to let the new, longer journey actually finish. DW-121 (the drain the drain switch never saw) is independently pinned by test/drain-switch-coverage.test.ts, which drives a ball down each outlane's own below-deck return channel through the real createMachine() pipeline and asserts s_drain makes before the ball parks in bd_trough -- verified red against the OLD (pre-fix) zone bounds and green against the live, widened one, reproducing this rework's own measured DW-121 evidence directly. Rework iteration 4 (2026-09-02, Story 2.1b narrow re-record exception): the press this golden is named for was RETIMED FOR THE NEW PLUNGE ROUTING -- the scenario did not change shape. Iteration 3 had deleted the press outright (transitions 1 -> 0) and declared the golden PARITY_INERT; that switched the AC 5 parity check off instead of satisfying it, and it is reverted here. The original press sat at tick 5041, timed for the pre-shot-map table's much shorter plunge-to-flipper travel; on the re-sited deflector the ball does not reach the left bat until tick ~8985, so the press moved 5041 -> 8956 with its release at 9556 (a 600-tick, 0.6 s hold, the same shape hold-and-release now uses), and durationTicks moved 8200 -> 10310. TRACE EVIDENCE that the press genuinely reaches the ball, measured against a paired control run of this identical golden with transitions removed (the idiom the covering test itself uses): (1) the ball's position is BIT-IDENTICAL to the control's for every tick up to and including t8985 (|delta pos| = 0), so nothing before the contact is doing the work; (2) the ball contacts the left flipper at t8986, its closest approach of the whole run -- 0.39 mm of clear air between ball surface and bat surface, centre 26.42 mm from the pivot at (170, 70) mm against a 13.495 mm ball radius plus a 12.5 mm base radius; (3) at that contact tick the bat is at 90.79 -> 92.08 deg (driven, at end of stroke) because of this press, where the control's bat sits still at 141.00 deg; (4) the ball leaves the contact at v = (217.4, 651.5, 512.6) mm/s against the control's (191.0, 682.0, 249.4) -- the lift more than doubled; (5) the ball then drains for real at t10282 against the control's t10344, and finalGameStateHash at the recorded durationTicks 10310 differs (30579b46 with the body, 11d6c2c0 without), which is the AC 5 parity check passing on its own terms rather than by exemption. The mechanism was isolated rather than assumed: control presses timed so the bat is back at its 141.00 deg rest pose and stationary by the contact tick (press@8500, @8540, @8600, each released after 200 ticks) leave the post-contact velocity unchanged at (190.9, 681.3, 249.4) and move the drain by only -6 ticks -- ordinary float drift -- while every press that changes the bat's pose AT the contact tick moves it by -62 to +1742. durationTicks 10310 is chosen inside [10282, 10343]: after this golden's own drain, and before the no-press control's, so the parity check is falsifiable by the body and the scenario claim (zero balls, ballsInPlay 0, full bd_trough) is satisfied by it.
